title: DayRecall — AI memory for your whole day | Apple Watch & iPhone
description: DayRecall listens on Apple Watch or iPhone during the hours you choose, turns what was said into text on your iPhone, and answers questions about your day.
og_title: DayRecall — AI memory for your whole day
og_description: Your Apple Watch, or just your iPhone, listens during the hours you choose and keeps what was said as text. Ask about your day any time.

app_description: An AI memory app for Apple Watch and iPhone. During the hours you choose it listens, keeps what was said as text on your iPhone, and answers questions about your day with the exact words.
app_features: Listens all day on Apple Watch, with no iPhone nearby; works with iPhone alone too
Speech becomes text on the iPhone; no audio is kept
Ask about your day and get the exact words, with the moment they were said
Marks who said what: Me, Other 1, Other 2
Follows conversations in up to three languages, translated into yours
Picks out to-dos, deadlines and meetings for you to confirm

Optional Health clues: inputs used by the App are kept in a protected local cache; Health labels and values are included in a recap sent to your API or a day shared with an AI app only if you choose to add them
No account and no DayRecall server; to-dos, recaps and answers use this iPhone by default, or your own API after you configure it and allow sharing

items.q: What is DayRecall?
items.a: DayRecall is an AI memory app for Apple Watch and iPhone, made for people who forget things. During the hours you choose, it listens, keeps what was said as text on your iPhone, and answers questions about your day with the exact words and where they came from.

items.q: Do I need an Apple Watch?
items.a: No. DayRecall works best with Apple Watch, and your iPhone can also listen on its own. When both listen, your day is one timeline, and what both heard is shown once.

items.q: Does DayRecall keep audio recordings?
items.a: Original audio is temporarily kept on your iPhone so you can correct a conversation’s language and process it again. It is then cleared automatically. You can delete a recording and its audio at any time; the text stays until you delete it.

items.q: Where is my data, and who can see it?
items.a: Your data is stored on your iPhone and in backups you choose to make. There is no account and no DayRecall server receiving your day. To-dos, recaps and answers use this iPhone by default. If you select and allow your own API, it receives new transcripts automatically for to-dos, a day’s conversations when you request a recap, and questions with matching excerpts. It may first receive a question alone to help search. You can also share a selected day with an AI app. These recipients use their own privacy rules; audio is never sent to the API.

items.q: What do I need to use DayRecall?
items.a: An iPhone with iOS 26 or later that supports Apple’s on-device speech recognition. An Apple Watch with watchOS 26 or later is optional. To-dos, recaps and answers use one AI engine: this iPhone’s model, which requires Apple Intelligence, or an OpenAI-compatible API that you configure and allow. Your API needs an internet connection.

items.q: Which iPhone models work?
items.a: DayRecall needs iOS 26 or later, which runs on iPhone 11 and later and iPhone SE (2nd generation) and later. Turning speech into text also needs Apple’s on-device speech recognition, which Apple doesn’t offer on some older models, including iPhone 11 models and iPhone SE (2nd generation), so we recommend iPhone 12 or later. If your iPhone can’t transcribe, DayRecall tells you. For to-dos, recaps and answers, the On this iPhone engine needs a device that supports Apple Intelligence. My own API can perform those three tasks without Apple Intelligence; transcription still requires the on-device speech recognition described above.

items.q: Which Apple Watch models work?
items.a: Any Apple Watch that runs watchOS 26 or later: Apple Watch Series 6 and later, Apple Watch SE (2nd generation) and later, and every Apple Watch Ultra. It needs to be paired with an iPhone that runs DayRecall. Apple Watch is optional: your iPhone can listen on its own.

items.q: Does my iPhone have to stay near my watch?
items.a: No. Your Apple Watch holds what it heard and hands it to your iPhone every two hours, or as soon as the two reconnect, for example when you get home in the evening.

items.q: Does it work without an internet connection?
items.a: Listening and transcription run on your devices. With On this iPhone selected and its required models downloaded and available, to-dos, recaps and answers also work offline. My own API needs an internet connection for those AI tasks. Places on the map also need a connection.

items.q: Why do the supported languages depend on Apple?
items.a: Transcription uses Apple’s on-device speech recognition, and translation uses Apple’s translation; their supported languages depend on the iPhone and iOS version. For to-dos, recaps and answers, On this iPhone uses Apple Intelligence and its supported languages. With My own API, language support depends on the service and model you choose. Choosing an API does not change transcription or translation support.

items.q: Which languages can DayRecall transcribe?
items.a: You can choose from English (US, UK), Chinese (Mandarin, China mainland), Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), Cantonese (China mainland), Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil, Portugal), Dutch, Swedish, Danish and Turkish. Each works only if Apple’s on-device speech recognition supports it on your iPhone; if it doesn’t, DayRecall marks the language as not supported. The first time you use a language, iOS downloads its speech model.

items.q: Which languages can it translate?
items.a: Lines in your other working languages can be translated into your main language with Apple’s on-device translation, so a pair of languages can be translated only if Apple supports it on your iPhone. Transcription support does not guarantee translation support, including for Cantonese. Check the available language pairs in DayRecall’s translation settings. iOS downloads each language before its first use. Apple lists the current languages on its feature availability page.

items.q: Which languages work for to-dos, recaps and answers?
items.a: It depends on the AI engine. On this iPhone uses Apple Intelligence, so its device, language and region requirements apply. If Apple Intelligence is unavailable, including where Apple does not offer it, you can choose My own API for all three tasks: to-dos, recaps and answers. Its supported languages depend on the service and model you choose. See Apple’s guide for the current Apple Intelligence requirements.

items.q: Which languages is the app in?
items.a: The app’s menus and screens come in 14 languages: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Portugal), Spanish, Swedish and Turkish. This is separate from the languages it can transcribe.

items.q: Can it follow a conversation in more than one language?
items.a: Yes. Turn on Multilingual transcription and add up to two more working languages: DayRecall follows a conversation that switches between them and transcribes each part in the language it was spoken in. Lines in the other languages can then be translated into your main language.

items.q: How do I start and stop listening?
items.a: Set your listening hours once, for example workdays from 9:00 to 18:00. When they begin, your Apple Watch asks whether to start: one tap, and it stops on its own when they end. You can also stop early, or skip a day.

items.q: What can I ask?
items.a: Anything about your day, in your own words: “What did Sam promise me today?” or “When is the report due?” Each answer shows where it came from, down to the line that was said.

items.q: How do to-dos work?
items.a: DayRecall picks out promises, deadlines and meetings from your day and waits for you to confirm them. Nothing reaches your calendar or Reminders until you say yes.

items.q: How does DayRecall tell voices apart?
items.a: Turn on Mark who is speaking and read five short cards aloud, about a minute. From then on, your lines are marked Me, and everyone else in a conversation gets a number: Other 1, Other 2 and so on. Your voiceprint stays on your iPhone, and no one else’s is kept. The feature is optional and off by default.

items.q: Can I hand a day to my own AI app?
items.a: Yes. Open Recap your day from Today, a past day or Ask. Write it here uses the AI engine you selected in Settings. To use another app, choose Hand to an AI app… and select it in the system share sheet; only the conversations you leave included go into the text file. To bring its to-dos back, copy the AI’s answer and tap Bring the AI’s answer back.

items.q: Can I import an audio file?
items.a: Yes. Import an audio file and DayRecall turns it into text on your iPhone, like everything else. It works on its own copy, so your original file stays as it is.

items.q: How much battery does it use?
items.a: Very little. Our in-house ultra-light speech model keeps only the moments when someone is talking. In internal testing on Apple Watch Series 11, listening added about 0.9% battery per hour.

items.q: How soon does the text appear?
items.a: Your watch hands over what it heard about every two hours, and when it stops listening, and your iPhone turns it into text as it arrives. For text sooner, open DayRecall and tap Sync now. In internal testing on iPhone 17 Pro Max, 3 minutes of conversation were processed in 17 seconds.

items.q: Does anything leave my iPhone?
items.a: With your own API selected and sharing allowed, new transcripts are sent automatically in batches to find to-dos, even when you are not asking questions. Write it here sends the selected day’s conversations to that service for a recap, including recorded places if present and Health labels and values only if you choose to add them. Questions send the question and matching excerpts; the question may first be sent alone to help search. Audio and your voiceprint are never sent to the API. You can also share a day with an AI app. Apple Maps and backups have their own data flows, explained in the Privacy Policy.

items.q: Does DayRecall read my Health data?
items.a: Only if you turn it on in Settings › Health. DayRecall reads sleep, steps and walking distance, workouts and heart rate to label parts of your day and find the times of activities you ask about. It never writes to Health or sends the inputs to us. Inputs used by the App are kept in a protected local cache, which can be included in a password-encrypted manual backup you create. On the recap and hand-over page, Add health data is off by default. Turning it on asks for permission and your choice is remembered. With it on, Health labels and activity times are included in a recap sent to your API or a day shared with an AI app; available heart rate, step, distance and duration values are included. Missing readings are left out. Health records are not attached to to-do or question requests. No medical conclusions or health advice are given.

items.q: Does DayRecall track me or show ads?
items.a: No. DayRecall has no ads, no analytics, no tracking and no third-party code that collects data. To help fix problems, it keeps a log on your devices of what it did, never what was said, for up to 14 days; the log leaves your iPhone only if you share it.

items.q: How do I delete my data?
items.a: Delete a recording, with its text and to-dos, from its page, or everything with Settings › Privacy › Delete all memories. Delete my voice removes your voiceprint. Deleting the app removes what it stored on your devices; copies in earlier backups stay until those backups are replaced.

items.q: Do I need to tell people DayRecall is listening?
items.a: Yes. Tell the people you talk with. Some places require everyone’s consent even when only text is kept, so follow the rules where you are; that responsibility is yours, as our Terms of Service explain.

items.q: How does the Mac app work with iPhone and Apple Watch?
items.a: Mac can record an in-person meeting or your microphone and a selected meeting app. Automatic transcription requires a supported Mac with macOS 26 or later. Pair your own iPhone to share saved text, meeting notes, titles, task updates and device status over an encrypted local network; keep both apps open. Audio assistance is enabled separately, and iCloud sharing is optional. Mac audio is removed after its transcript is saved; failed transcription keeps audio for retry.

items.q: How can I back up my library?
items.a: In Settings, export a local library file or use the optional private iCloud backup. The local file has no password and can include saved Health and Calendar inputs, so store it somewhere you trust. The in-app iCloud backup excludes these inputs and saved recaps. Restoring replaces the current library and supported settings. Deleting local data does not delete exported files or cloud copies; remove those separately.

items.q: Can I save a recap to Notion or Obsidian?
items.a: Set up a destination in Settings › Third-party connections, then choose and confirm it on a saved recap. Nothing is sent automatically. Notion receives the recap directly to create a child page. Obsidian uses a device-only clipboard copy that expires after two minutes and opens a dated note; check Obsidian to confirm it was saved. Disconnecting or deleting a recap in DayRecall does not delete copies already in those apps.

items.q: Where can I get DayRecall?
items.a: Download it from the App Store. It runs on iPhone, and Apple Watch is optional.

items.q: How much does DayRecall cost?
items.a: DayRecall is free to download from the App Store. Try everything free for 3 days, then unlock it with one in-app purchase; the App Store shows the price for your country before you buy. Every future update is included: there is no subscription and nothing renews. If you got DayRecall before November 7, 2026 (UTC), it is already fully unlocked.

items.q: Is DayRecall still being worked on?
items.a: Yes. Every version is written up on What’s new, newest first, with the date it came out. Unlock it once, and every future update is included.

items.q: How do I get help?
items.a: Write to support@dayrecall.com and tell us when it happened and on which device. A log helps most: Settings › Developer options › Logs › Share log.

1.4.3.title: Free to download: try it, then unlock it once
1.4.3.lead: The first App Store version since 0.2.32, with everything from 0.2.33 to 1.4.2 below.

groups.title: Price and unlock
items: Free to download. Start with a 3-day trial of everything, then unlock DayRecall with one purchase. No subscription, no automatic charge.
The trial starts when you tap “Start free 3-day trial” and Apple confirms it, and runs for 72 hours in a row. Reinstalling, a new phone or restoring purchases doesn’t restart it.
One purchase unlocks DayRecall on iPhone and Apple Watch.
If you got DayRecall before November 7 (UTC), as a paid or a free download, it is fully unlocked for you: no trial, nothing more to pay.

After the trial, new recordings, audio imports and new AI tasks need the unlock. What you have already captured stays yours to view, search, export and delete, and recordings already on your watch still arrive and turn into text.

groups.title: Fixes
items: A line corrected on another device no longer keeps its old translation; it waits for a new one.
Meeting notes are written again when more of the meeting turns into text or a line is corrected.
A meeting started on your iPhone keeps your Apple Watch listening until it ends, even past your listening hours (up to 12 hours).

1.4.2.title: Start your watch from your iPhone

groups.title: Today and Apple Watch
items: When your Apple Watch is connected but not listening, the first button on the listening card is “Start on Apple Watch”, and the iPhone one becomes “Record on iPhone instead”. The watch card in Devices has the same button.
After you tap it, raise your wrist and open DayRecall on the watch: it starts by itself, and the hint goes away once the watch is listening.
One tap counts once: if you open the watch more than 5 minutes later, or the watch stopped in between, it doesn’t start by itself.

groups.title: My voice
items: All five voice cards are now read from a script; none asks you to answer in your own words.
With multilingual transcription on, cards 4 and 5 are in your other working languages. Cantonese has its own spoken script.

groups.title: Recordings and Library
items: On a recording’s page (Library › Recordings), while its audio is still kept (for 24 hours after recording), tap a line to play from there; the line playing is marked.
Touch and hold a line to copy it.
A day opened from Library shows its date at the top; tap Library again to go back to its front page.

groups.title: Privacy policy and terms
items: The privacy policy and terms inside the app now have the Mac, meeting and Apple Watch sections in the other 12 languages.

1.4.1.title: Meetings when you want them, clearer places

groups.title: Apple Watch
items: When it isn’t listening, the two buttons are “Listen all day” and “Meeting”. “Meeting” appears once Meetings is on in Settings on your iPhone.
A meeting starts at once, in the language chosen in Settings; tap “Meeting · language” during the meeting to switch.
When your watch notes places, its listening screen says so; if its location permission is off, it tells you where to turn it on.

groups.title: Meetings
items: A new Meetings switch in Settings › Features, off by default. Turn it on, then choose the language meetings start in under “Meeting language”, where you can also add languages.
On Today, “Start a meeting” sits beside “Record on iPhone” and no longer asks for a language; tap its label during a meeting to switch.

groups.title: Places
items: “Places from” is now one row: open it to choose iPhone or Apple Watch.
My places: Home, Work and the other kinds are kinds, not names, and two places of one kind are told apart by their street.
The address found is kept. If it’s slightly off, drag the map to move the place a little (up to 250 m) or correct the house number. Your own name for it is optional.
Places named with those words before become kinds.

groups.title: DayRecall for Mac (beta)
items: Fixes the Mac app freezing right after it opens on macOS 27.

1.4.0.title: Pause the watch, meetings and named places

groups.title: Apple Watch
items: One screen shows its state, with two round buttons: pause and end.
Pause for 15 minutes, 30 minutes or an hour and it picks up by itself, never past your listening hours; hold to end the day.

groups.title: Meetings
items: Start a meeting on your iPhone or your watch and choose its language; it shows as its own stretch on the timeline.
After three hours, your watch asks whether you’re still in the meeting.
When it ends you can get meeting notes. If they come from your own API, DayRecall asks for your permission for that separately.
A meeting is the same one on your iPhone and your Mac.

groups.title: Places
items: Several stays at one spot become one place. A name that can’t be found is tried again, and shows as “Unnamed place” if it still can’t.
Name a place on the map and set how far it reaches (Settings › My places): later stays there get its name, and it goes into your backups.
Your watch can note places while it listens (off until you turn it on); its location then stands in for your iPhone’s.

groups.title: My voice
items: Add up to four people you often talk with (a name and how you know them); their names appear on the timeline, the poster and the text you export.

groups.title: Quicker ways in
items: Touch and hold the app icon for Ask, To-dos and Recap.
“View Settings” on a notification opens the app’s own notification settings.

groups.title: First-time setup
items: The map, Health and who-is-speaking switches start off; turn them on when you want them.

groups.title: DayRecall for Mac (beta)
items: A real Mac window: a sidebar, a compact list of records, a details column, a month calendar, search by word, sharing and a menu bar item. You can also export and import records.
Steadier syncing between devices on a poor network: meeting notes now sync, and a phone that walks away no longer ties up the connection.

groups.title: Fix
items: If you had recorded your own voice, opening “Recap your day” could freeze the screen, or the app was closed when you came back to it and had to be swiped away. That no longer happens.
People who never recorded their voice were not affected.

groups.title: Settings
items: Meeting language now sits under Multilingual transcription and is called “Meeting language”. It appears once you have a second working language: one row, Off or one of your languages.
With multilingual transcription off, your watch no longer shows a meeting-language button you can’t use, and your earlier choice is kept.
Listening hours take one row per day (day, time, switch); a day you turn on reuses the hours of the listening day before it.
Change one day’s time and you’re asked whether every listening day should match; one tap applies it.
Advanced Settings is a short list in three parts, Listening, Detection and Data; open one to adjust it. Explanations for sliders and switches sit behind an “i”.
Data and Backups has a new look, and before you export a backup with Health data, one card sums up the three things to know.
Detailed logging can stay on until you turn it off (by default it turns off after 24 hours).

groups.title: Fixes
items: The recap page no longer freezes the screen.
Stalled Apple Watch transfers are retried.
A compatibility problem with library backups.

groups.title: My voice
items: My voice uses a new voice model. Record your voice once more after updating; earlier speaker labels stay.

groups.title: Languages
items: Language detection listens to six seconds of speech by default; choose three or six seconds in Advanced Settings.

groups.title: Backup and restore
items: Export your library as a file or back it up to your own private iCloud, and restore it later.
Health and calendar history brought in from a backup is kept apart and never passes for the new phone’s own data.

groups.title: Fixes
items: Problems when you withdraw consent for your API or cancel a request.
Your edits survive while a conversation is transcribed again.

groups.title: Languages
items: Every screen, the new ones too, is in all 14 languages: device connections, the model directory, permission notes, the poster, the purchase screens and more.
The offline privacy notes in all 14 languages match the website: how long audio is kept, language correction, and how exported and backup copies are kept.

groups.title: Smoother and more accurate
items: Switching days is smoother, with less repeated counting and map work.
Speaking time counts only the parts where someone actually talks.
A silent recording ends normally and no longer says the transcription is done.

groups.title: DayRecall for Mac (beta)
items: Transcription languages match the iPhone’s 17 choices, tell Simplified and Traditional Chinese apart, and follow your region.

groups.title: Daily poster
items: Three looks and a line you pick from your day, saved as a picture or a short video.
You can also make one with Shortcuts.

groups.title: Edit conversations
items: Rename a conversation, edit a line or bring back the original text.
While the audio is still there, change a conversation’s language to transcribe it again; pick the meeting language right on your Apple Watch.

groups.title: Connections and reading
items: Save recaps to Notion or Obsidian.
With your own API, the model directory can be updated; it only goes online when you tap.
Open the website and the legal documents inside the app.

groups.title: DayRecall for Mac (beta)
items: A real library on the Mac: record in-person or online meetings, pause and resume them, and manage meetings, records and to-dos.
Works with your paired iPhone and Apple Watch over your local network.

groups.title: Fixes
items: The watch showing it was listening after it had stopped.
Stop reminders being withdrawn too early.

groups.title: DayRecall for Mac (beta)
items: DayRecall for Mac joins the beta: a native window, meeting text you can import, and meetings kept in their own place.
Once paired, a Mac with its language model ready can transcribe for your iPhone over an encrypted local connection and send the text back; if the Mac can’t, your iPhone does it.
Meeting text on the Mac can sync through your own private iCloud, once you turn it on.

groups.title: Trial and purchase (beta)
items: The beta gets the 3-day trial and the one-time unlock so the purchase flow can be tested; nothing is charged in the beta.
Before a trial starts, DayRecall checks that speech and your chosen AI are ready; if not, the clock doesn’t start.

groups.title: About
items: Rate DayRecall, share it or open the website from About.

groups.title: After an interruption
items: After an alarm, a call or Siri, DayRecall keeps trying for about a minute and picks up recording by itself; it only tells you if it can’t.

The “Listening paused” reminder no longer comes at once: it waits until the microphone has been free for 20 seconds without recording resuming, and repeats once 5 minutes later. If recording comes back on its own, nothing rings.
While an alarm is still ringing or a call is still going, you aren’t reminded halfway through.
The iPhone’s “Apple Watch stopped recording” notice waits the same way and goes away once the watch is listening again.
Choose when reminders come in Settings › Listening hours › If recording pauses.

groups.title: Ask and the timeline
items: Better at questions about what you were doing, like “what did we talk about while I was running?”; if the first search finds nothing, it tries once more in other words.
Short walks on the timeline are no longer hidden behind long conversations.

groups.title: Languages
items: The screens and offline legal documents are complete in all 14 languages.

0.2.32.title: Download it from the App Store
items: On the App Store from 30 October, with everything in the versions below.
Fixes a crash at launch in 0.2.31.

groups.title: Recap your day
items: Written in the background: leave the page or switch tabs while it works. A thin bar above every tab shows the step and the time left, and you can stop at any moment.
A finished recap is kept with its day. On Today the row says “Your recap · written at …”; tap to read it, then copy, share, send its list to To confirm, write it again or delete it.
Before it starts you see roughly how long it will take; over a minute, it first explains that you can leave the page, that DayRecall needs to stay open, and the quicker ways.
Stopping and starting again, or retrying after a failure, doesn’t read the parts already read.
When the app isn’t in front or the iPhone is warm, the on-device model waits, and carries on once you’re back and it has cooled down.
If you’ve left the app when it’s done, a silent notification says your recap is ready (turn it off in Settings › Notifications).

groups.title: Ask a stronger AI
items: Not good enough? Hand the day to an AI app and bring its answer back: it’s kept with the day, next to the iPhone’s own recap.
When this iPhone can’t write a recap (no Apple Intelligence, turned off, model still downloading, or your API not set up), it says why and shows the two other ways.

groups.title: Recap every day
items: Settings › AI engine › Recap every day: Remind me (the default), Write it for me, or Off.
“Remind me” sends a silent notification half an hour after your listening hours end, if the day has over 5 minutes of speech and no recap yet.

groups.title: Reminders and reliability
items: When your listening hours begin, your watch reminds you once; if nothing has started 20 minutes later, your iPhone reminds you again, and both go away once recording starts.
Ask finishes on time even when the model is slow to answer, and a late recap can’t come back after you’ve cleared your library.

groups.title: More reliable recording
items: iPhone recording recovers by itself after an interruption; Apple Watch transfers are retried, and deleted recordings don’t come back.
If a recording that arrives from an offline watch can’t be placed before or after something you deleted, it’s kept apart for you to restore or delete.
A stop that wasn’t registered is registered later; once the speech model is installed, waiting recordings are transcribed, older months too, and their translations become searchable.

groups.title: Today
items: The first screen is for your day: the listening card keeps only the state, today’s speaking time and the record button, with a small warning only when something needs you.
“Recap your day” is a small row you can close, and a button at the top still opens it.
Quiet stretches with no words found no longer notify you; transcription progress and failures you can retry are in Settings › Devices.

groups.title: Settings and first-time setup
items: Settings is the last tab, grouped into General, Features, Help and About; advanced options have their own page, with explanations behind an “i”.
In first-time setup, choose what DayRecall keeps track of.
Setting your watch to come back to DayRecall when you raise your wrist takes four numbered steps.

groups.title: To-dos and reminders
items: To-dos and your Reminders stay in step: no duplicate reminders, and completion syncs.
When listening ends, you’re reminded to sync and told roughly when the text will be ready; from the second day waiting to sync, the reminder can make a sound.

groups.title: Health
items: Health on the timeline has a new look, and a day with only a workout shows it too.

When you hand a day to an AI app or write a recap with your own API, you can add Health labels and values (heart rate, steps, distance and more). It’s off by default, and missing values are never turned into zeros.

groups.title: AI and privacy
items: With your own API, choose the model and how hard it reasons.
Once you allow your API, it’s used to find to-dos, write recaps and answer questions; audio is never sent, and you’re asked again before more is shared.
If saving an API key fails, the old key is kept and you’re told.
Read the terms and the privacy policy offline in the app, in all 14 languages.

groups.title: Sample day
items: The sample day has speakers, walks, workouts, heart rate and translations, and takes you from a to-do back to the words and the moment.

ask.title: Ask your memory
ask.sub: Anything you recorded, or anything at all.
ask.s1: What deadlines are coming up this week?
ask.s2: What did we agree on in yesterday’s meeting?
ask.question: What did Sam promise me today?
ask.a1: Sam will send you the copy on Wednesday.
ask.a2: You will send Sam the quote by Friday.
ask.snip1: I’ll send you the copy on Wednesday.
ask.snip2: Sure, I’ll send it on Friday.
ask.row0: Great. When can I have the copy?

steps.c: Type a question about anything you recorded, or tap one of the suggestions.
The answer comes from your recordings. Each number points to the recording it came from.
Tap a source to see the line that was said, marked in the transcript.

todos.l0: Can you send me the quote by Friday?
todos.l1: Sure, I'll send it on Friday.

steps.c: DayRecall finds to-dos, promises and meetings in what was said, and marks the lines they came from.
They wait in To confirm. Tap the check mark to accept a to-do, and it goes to Reminders.
A meeting opens the system’s add-event sheet, where you choose the calendar. Nothing is added until you confirm.

places.show: Show the day on a map
places.alertTitle: Show the day on a map?
places.alertMessage: This uses some extra battery. Next, iOS asks for location access: choose Always, so places are noted while DayRecall is closed.

steps.c: Turn on Show the day on a map. iOS then asks for location access: choose Always, so places are noted while DayRecall is closed.
Each part of the day shows where it was said. The places you stayed at are numbered in the order you reached them.
Tap a place to see it on the map, and what was said there.

a.line: Can you send me the quote by Friday?

c.line: Let’s push the launch to Friday.

d.line: Sam said the quote is fine.

steps.c: Each part of the day sits on a timeline, newest first, with the quiet stretches in between.
Tap any day of the week to see how it went, or swipe back to earlier weeks.
Search finds the words in every conversation you’ve kept.

week.title: Pick what goes on your calendar

t2.title: Sam sends the copy on Wednesday

steps.c: Every deadline and promise coming up in the next seven days, from what you heard. Nothing is added yet.

steps.t: Pick what goes on your calendar
steps.c: Everything starts ticked. Untick what you don’t want.
Tap Add. The ticked ones go to your calendar and Reminders; what you left unticked stays in To confirm.

cards.line: Morning, did you see the quote?

bullets: Quote agreed; send it by Monday.
handoff.promisedToYouItem: Sam sends the copy on Wednesday

steps.c: Tap “Hand to an AI app”. The day’s conversations and your question become one text file.
Pick the AI app you use in the sheet that opens. The file goes along, ready to send.
A few seconds later: the recap, your to-dos, who promised what.

health.label: Health
health.show: Show sleep, activity and heart rate
health.found: Found data from the last 7 days.
health.note: Read only. Health information is kept in a protected cache on this iPhone and is not sent to us. Health labels and values go to your API or an AI app only if you choose to add them to a recap or shared day. Adding Health data is off by default.
health.factDetail: Heart rate around 96 · resting heart rate about 62
health.question: What did we talk about before bed?
health.answer: You planned a hike for this weekend.

steps.c: Off until you turn it on. Then DayRecall reads sleep, steps, workouts and heart rate from the Health app. Read only.
A part of the day can say you were walking, just after a workout, or had a heart rate faster than usual. Open it to see the numbers.

steps.t: Ask by what you were doing
steps.c: Ask about before bed or while you were running, and DayRecall looks in those times.
How long you talked, a name for the day, and when the talking happened. No words from your conversations, unless you add a line.
Pick one line from the day, or write your own. Only the line you picked goes on the poster.
Choose a look, then share a picture or a short video. The QR code in the corner can be swapped for the web address or the name alone.

features_17: Share a day as a picture or a short video: how long you talked, a name for the day, and a line you pick. Nothing else that was said goes on it.
health_02: Sometimes you remember by what you were doing
health_03: Turn it on and DayRecall reads your sleep, walks, workouts and heart rate from the Health app. They become clues on your day: a conversation can say it happened while you were walking, just after a workout, or with a heart rate faster than usual.
health_04: Labels on your timeline: walking, working out, asleep, heart rate above usual
health_05: Ask “What did we talk about before bed?” or “What did I say while I was running?”
health_06: Off until you turn it on. Read only: DayRecall never writes to Health.
health_07: Read only. Health information is kept in a protected cache on this iPhone and is not sent to us. Health labels and values go to your API or an AI app only if you choose to add them to a recap or shared day. Adding Health data is off by default.
health_09: Animation: the Health switch is turned on, the timeline shows a walk and a heart rate above usual, and a question about before bed finds what was said.
